speaker: Carl Olson
words: Well, it was my brother Albert and Bob and Oscar and a fellow named Chester Hilliard, they went hunting together. They went down to the Bear Creek Falls, that's five, six miles from home. See, and they had the single gauge shotgun, 12 gauge, my brother, I don't know what the others had, and he shot one bird, you know, and then he put another shell in, single shot, you know, and then there was a big boulder and he walked down that boulder and he hit the hammer in the boulder and he fell down in the creek and my brother Albert was right back of him, shots just missed him, just cut about four or five inches long and about an inch and a half wide here. If the bear had been farther away, it would have killed him because then the shots would have spread, but the bear was so close here that the wad, you know, they held the shots together, they didn't get time to spread. See, that's what made such a long streak.

speaker: Sam Schrager
words: So, what happened? What happened then?

speaker: Carl Olson
words: Well, he fell off the rock when the creek was running right below there and Bob and Hilliard would come home and told about it and Albert stayed with him, but they thought he was dead because he fainted just as they left, but they didn't mention that when they got home, and then the first thing you know, here they come with him and the doctor come from the town the same time. I don't know how they could connect that up. See that Bear Creek Falls, you know where Little Bear is? Well, Little Bear runs here and down there's the falls and here's where we live. Here's the falls, and they carried them up on Little Bear and then somebody must have went to Troy and told the doctor to come out and how we could find where we lived. I don't know either because everyone knows what roads are right, but of course, they can ask neighbors. Neighbors were pretty close, so he came about the same time as you think one person went clear into town.

speaker: Sam Schrager
words: You were telling the kids that you thought maybe maybe they relayed the word to the neighbor.

speaker: Carl Olson
words: Yeah, they had to relay them, but they had to go to the including taller where you had to go to the place every time, you know, with no telephone. And then there was a phone fella named Dan Tullson, and he's the one that got the doctor. He hitched his horse up, lived about four miles from town, I think, so he drove down there right away then.

speaker: Sam Schrager
words: So probably a couple, this whoever relayed the message went to Dan Tullson's place.

speaker: Carl Olson
words: Yeah, and that's the way they had to get by the whole state, they had to relay it to your neighbor. And the houses wasn't too far from the roads in those days, you know, when they built the roads, they'd be pretty close to the house, so they didn't have to walk too far to relay anything.

speaker: Sam Schrager
words: So your brother was carried, they carried him, they carry your brother all the way home?

speaker: Carl Olson
words: Yeah, not all the way, they carried him from about half a mile. The road come, we lived here, we say, and the road come, and then the road went around this way, and this way they get home. So they took the shortcut, carried him, only about a quarter mile, and instead of driving four or five feet, you know, from the rock to the water, head first, you see.

speaker: Sam Schrager
words: Well, what did the doctor do when he got there?

speaker: Carl Olson
words: Well, all he done, I can think of, I've seen him, he brought out a scissor, and he was meat slivers hanging, you know, he trimmed her off, flicking clean, and then I believe he put sulfur on it, and then he put a rag over, and I believe he come back only once after that, and the Ma took care of it all together, he just kept putting on there. So you see how he got along, don't they? Of course, I don't know, I was liked some way when I was a kid, everybody want me to come to their place and stay, they wanted to adopt me, and Hillary, he had to have me there all the time, I'm the one that blowed the horn, I told you about that, and you scared the cows all to death.

speaker: Sam Schrager
words: What was that story now? I don't remember that much, I think you mentioned it to me once, but I don't.

speaker: Carl Olson
words: Well, old Hilliard, his dad lived in Lewiston, you know, and he rode horseback down there, it took two days to make the trip, you know, horseback, so I was all alone up there in the house with the, and I got so lonesome, I was sitting there, and I seen the lamb sitting there, I was ashamed, I thought, blowed him, and the cows come from all directions, with their tails in the air, belly aching, and you wish they couldn't get into the house because of the fans around it, and then I figured out why it was, it was a disaster called, you know, the wild animals got there just like we have, and they thought we was more bringing another cow, you know, they smelled the blood, that's what made them do that, there was blood around, there was blood around, no, but the better that way, because we butchered him one time, and a bull rubbed, he made that same old sound, you know.

speaker: Sam Schrager
words: But what did you do?... With all the cows all trying to get in the house…

speaker: Carl Olson
words: I quit afterwards, they couldn't get in because of the fans around, they would have tried to get into the house, I suppose, yeah, that's,… i missed it because we used to go and get our cows down the canyon when we were younger, whole lot, you know, and we had to walk down them steep hills and hunt them up and chase them home, if I had had this whistle, I could have sat up and decided, they didn't blow it, and they wouldn't come, you know, to see where the danger was,… yeah, that was pretty good, all animals got caught like that, I believe, I was out hunting pheasants, you know, kinks, they call here, and I wounded the she-kink in the wings, that you couldn't fly, you're jumping on the ground and making a funny racket, and you ought to see the roosters come in, five or six of them come, flew around there, they heard that noise, see, that was a signal, something like that, she says, you know, so I thought to myself, if I could make a caller like that, I could go out and get a lot of birds, no, I didn't think it was any birds around there at all, hardly when I was four or five, at least, roosters come from someplace to see what was wrong, and that's the way it is with putting in all animals, I never did try the horn, I used to go out hunting elk and deer quite a bit, before I had one of them, I could have maybe called the elk and deer to us too, but it just never come to my mind.
